title.zh: 卷四 本紀第四 少帝
title.raw: 卷四 本紀第四 少帝 Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Shao

sentences.zh: 永初三年五月癸亥，武帝崩，是日，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On the day guihai in the fifth month of the third year Yongchu, Emperor Wu died; that same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the fifth month of Yongchu year 3, Emperor Wu died; that same day the crown prince took the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后曰太皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申，以尚書僕射傅亮為中書監，司空徐羨之、領軍將軍謝晦及亮輔政。

translations.literal: On the day renshen in the sixth month, Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Director of the Palace Secretariat; the Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, the General Who Leads the Army Xie Hui, and Liang were appointed to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renshen, Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Director of the Palace Secretariat; Xu Xianzhi, Minister of Works, Xie Hui, General Who Leads the Army, and Liang were named regents.

sentences.zh: 戊子，太尉長沙王道憐薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the Grand Marshal, Prince of Changsha Dao Ling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Grand Marshal Prince of Changsha Dao Ling died.

sentences.zh: 秋九月丁未，有司奏武皇帝配南郊，武敬皇后配北郊。

translations.literal: In autumn, on the day dingwei in the ninth month, the relevant offices memorialized that Emperor Wu be paired at the southern suburb and Empress Wu Jing be paired at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, on dingwei, the relevant offices reported that Emperor Wu should be honored at the southern suburb and Empress Wu Jing at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月戊午，有星孛于營室。

translations.literal: In winter, on the day wuwu in the eleventh month, a broom star appeared in the Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on wuwu, a comet appeared in the Encampment constellation.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚戌，魏軍克滑臺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, Wei forces captured Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengxu, Wei forces took Huatai.

sentences.zh: 明年春正月己亥朔，大赦，改元為景平元年。

translations.literal: On the new moon of the first month of spring in the following year, on the day jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to the inaugural year Jingping.
translations.idiomatic: At the new moon of the first month of spring the next year, on jihai, there was a general amnesty and the reign title was changed to Jingping year 1.

sentences.zh: 文武進位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，祀南郊。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the southern suburb was sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, sacrifices were offered at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: [3]虜將達奚卬破金墉，進圍虎牢。

translations.literal: [3] A barbarian general, Daxi Ang, broke Jin Yong and advanced to besiege Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: [3] The enemy general Daxi Ang took Jin Yong and pressed on to besiege Hulao.

sentences.zh: [4]毛德祖擊虜敗之，虜退而復合。

translations.literal: [4] Mao Dezu struck the barbarians and defeated them; the barbarians withdrew and then gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Mao Dezu attacked the enemy and defeated them; they withdrew, then rallied again.

sentences.zh: 拓跋木末又遣安平公涉歸寇青州。

translations.literal: Tuoba Mumo also sent the Duke of Anping, Shegui, to raid Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Mumo also sent Duke of Anping Shegui to raid Qing Province.

sentences.zh: [5]癸卯，河南郡失守。

translations.literal: [5] On the day maoyin, Henan Commandery was lost.
translations.idiomatic: [5] On maoyin, Henan Commandery fell.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，有星孛于東壁。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, a broom star appeared in the Eastern Wall.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, a comet appeared in the Eastern Wall.

sentences.zh: 二月丁丑，太皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day dingchou, the grand empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingchou, the grand empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜、吐谷渾阿犲並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun and Tuyuhun Aqi both sent envoys to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun and Tuyuhun Aqi both sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，[6]爵蒙遜為驃騎大將軍，[7]封河西王。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, [6] Mengxun was enfeoffed as General of Agile Cavalry, [7] and made Prince of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, [6] Mengxun was enfeoffed as General of Agile Cavalry [7] and created Prince of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 以阿犲為安西將軍、沙州刺史，封澆河公。

translations.literal: Aqi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Liang Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: Aqi was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Liang Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qiaohe.

sentences.zh: 辛未，富陽人孫法光反，[8]寇山陰，會稽太守褚淡之遣山陰令陸劭討敗之。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Sun Faguang of Fuyang rebelled, [8] raided Shanyin; the Governor of Kuaiji Chu Danzhi sent the Magistrate of Shanyin Lu Shao to attack and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Sun Faguang of Fuyang rose in revolt [8] and raided Shanyin; Kuaiji governor Chu Danzhi sent Shanyin magistrate Lu Shao to defeat him.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 9.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 9.

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅，孝懿皇后祔葬于興寧陵。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renyin, Empress Xiao Yi was enshrined and buried at Xingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renyin, Empress Xiao Yi was enshrined at Xingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 是月，高麗國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That month, the state of Goguryeo sent envoys to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Goguryeo sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 甲子，豫州刺史劉粹遣軍襲許昌，殺虜潁川太守庾龍。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the Inspector of Yu Province Liu Cui sent troops in a surprise attack on Xuchang and killed the barbarian Administrator of Yingchuan Yu Long.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Yu inspector Liu Cui sent troops to raid Xuchang and killed the enemy Yingchuan administrator Yu Long.

sentences.zh: [10]乙丑，虜騎寇高平。

translations.literal: [10] On the day yichou, barbarian horsemen raided Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: [10] On yichou, enemy horsemen raided Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 初虜自河北之敗，請修和親；

translations.literal: Earlier, after their defeat north of the Yellow River, the barbarians had requested a marriage alliance;
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat north of the Yellow River, the northerners had sought a peace marriage;

sentences.zh: 及聞高祖崩，因復侵擾，河、洛之地騷然矣。

translations.literal: when they heard that Gaozu had died, they again invaded and harassed; the lands of the Yellow and Luo rivers were thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: but when they learned that Gaozu had died, they invaded again; the Yellow and Luo regions were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，檀道濟北征，次臨朐，焚虜攻具。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Tan Daoji marched north on campaign, halted at Linqu, and burned the barbarians’ siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Tan Daoji marched north, camped at Linqu, and burned the enemy siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏軍克虎牢，執司州刺史毛德祖以歸。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Wei forces captured Hulao and took the Inspector of Si Province Mao Dezu back with them.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Wei forces took Hulao and carried off Si inspector Mao Dezu.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉，尊所生張夫人為皇太后。

translations.literal: In autumn, on the day guiyou in the seventh month, his birth mother Lady Zhang was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on guiyou, his birth mother Lady Zhang was made empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以旱，詔赦五歲刑以下罪人。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, because of drought, an edict pardoned offenders sentenced to five years or less.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, owing to drought, an edict pardoned those sentenced to five years or less.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 11.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 11.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己未，有星孛于氐，指尾，貫攝提，向大角，仲月在危，季月掃天倉而後滅。

translations.literal: In winter, on the day jiwei in the tenth month, a broom star appeared in Di; it pointed toward Wei, pierced Sheti, and turned toward Great Horn; in the second month of the season it was in Wei, in the last month it swept the Celestial Granary and then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiwei, a comet appeared in Di, aimed at Wei, crossed Sheti, and turned toward Great Horn; in mid-season it stood in Wei, in the last month it swept the Celestial Granary, then disappeared.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏主拓跋嗣薨，子燾立。

translations.literal: That year, the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died and his son Tao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Wei ruler Tuoba Si died and his son Tao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，[12]省寧州之江陽、犍為、安上三郡，合為宋昌郡。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin in the twelfth month, [12] the three commanderies Jiangyang, Qianwei, and Anshang in Ning Province were abolished and merged into Songchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the twelfth month, [12] Ning Province’s Jiangyang, Qianwei, and Anshang commanderies were abolished and merged into Songchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月癸巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the new moon of the second month of spring, on the day guisi, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, at the new moon of the second month of spring, on guisi, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: [13]廢南豫州刺史廬陵王義真為庶人，徙新安郡。

translations.literal: [13] The Prince of Luling Yizhen, Inspector of South Yu Province, was deposed as a commoner and moved to Xin’an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: [13] South Yu inspector Prince of Luling Yizhen was deposed to commoner status and exiled to Xin’an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以皇弟義恭為冠軍將軍，南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, the emperor’s younger brother Yigong was made General Who Crowns the Army and Inspector of South Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the emperor’s younger brother Yigong was made General Who Crowns the Army and South Yu inspector.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大風，[14]天有五色雲，占者以為有兵。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, a great wind blew; [14] the sky showed five-colored clouds; diviners took it to portend war.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, a great wind rose; [14] five-colored clouds appeared in the sky, and diviners read them as a sign of war.

sentences.zh: 高麗國遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: The state of Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 執政使使者誅義真于新安。

translations.literal: The regents sent an envoy to execute Yizhen at Xin’an.
translations.idiomatic: The regents sent an agent to have Yizhen put to death at Xin’an.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，江州刺史王弘、南兗州刺史檀道濟入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, the Inspector of Jiang Province Wang Hong and the Inspector of South Yan Province Tan Daoji entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, Jiang inspector Wang Hong and South Yan inspector Tan Daoji came to court.

sentences.zh: [15]帝居處所為多過失。

translations.literal: [15] In his daily conduct the emperor committed many faults.
translations.idiomatic: [15] In his daily conduct the emperor committed many faults.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，皇太后令曰：

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, the empress dowager issued an order, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the empress dowager issued an order, saying:

sentences.zh: 王室不造，天禍未悔，先帝創業弗永，棄世登遐。

translations.literal: The royal house is ill-fated; Heaven’s calamity has not yet relented; the late emperor’s founding work did not long endure, and he has left the world and ascended far away.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house is ill-fated; Heaven’s wrath has not yet lifted; the late emperor’s founding work did not long endure, and he has departed this world.

sentences.zh: 義符長嗣，屬當天位，不謂窮凶極悖，一至於此。

translations.literal: Yifu, as eldest son, was fit to occupy the heavenly throne; who would have thought his wickedness and perversity would reach this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu, as eldest son, was fit for the throne; none could have imagined his wickedness would reach this extreme.

sentences.zh: 大行在殯，宇內哀惶，幸災肆於悖詞，喜容表於在慼。

translations.literal: While the late emperor lay in coffin and all within the four seas mourned in fear, he took disaster as occasion for reckless words and showed a pleased countenance amid grief.
translations.idiomatic: While the late emperor still lay in state and the realm mourned, he spoke recklessly as though rejoicing in calamity and showed pleasure amid grief.

sentences.zh: 至乃徵召樂府，鳩集伶官，優倡管絃，靡不備奏，珍羞甘膳，有加平日。

translations.literal: He even summoned the Music Office, gathered players, and had singers, actors, pipes, and strings all perform without exception; rare delicacies and sweet fare exceeded those of ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: He even summoned the Music Office, gathered players, and had singers, actors, and musicians perform without stint; delicacies exceeded those of ordinary days.

sentences.zh: 採擇媵御，產子就宮，靦然無怍，醜聲四達。

translations.literal: He selected concubines, and when they bore children he brought them into the palace, utterly without shame; ugly reports spread in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: He selected concubines and, when they bore children, brought them into the palace without shame; scandal spread in every direction.

sentences.zh: 及懿后崩背，重加天罰，親與左右執紼歌呼，推排梓宮，抃掌笑謔，殿省備聞。

translations.literal: When Empress Yi died, Heaven added a further punishment: he personally, with those at his side, took mourning cords and sang and shouted, pushed about the inner coffin, clapped his hands and laughed and jested—the palace offices all heard it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yi died, he heaped Heaven’s punishment upon grief: he personally took mourning cords with his attendants and sang and shouted, pushed the inner coffin about, clapped his hands and laughed—the whole palace heard it.

sentences.zh: 加復日夜媟狎，羣小慢戲，興造千計，費用萬端，帑藏空虛，人力殫盡。

translations.literal: Moreover, day and night he indulged in lewd intimacy; petty men treated him with disrespectful sport; constructions ran to a thousand schemes and expenses to ten thousand outlets; the treasury was emptied and manpower exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he indulged in lewd sport; petty men mocked him; constructions multiplied and expenses soared; the treasury was emptied and the people exhausted.

sentences.zh: 刑罰苛虐，幽囚日增。

translations.literal: Punishments were harsh and cruel; prisoners in confinement increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments grew harsh and cruel; prisoners increased daily.

sentences.zh: 居帝王之位，好皁隸之役，處萬乘之尊，悅廝養之事。

translations.literal: Though he occupied the emperor’s place, he delighted in menial tasks; though he possessed the honor of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler, he took pleasure in stable-boy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though he sat on the imperial throne, he delighted in menial labor; though he held supreme rank, he took pleasure in stable-boy tasks.

sentences.zh: 親執鞭撲，毆擊無辜，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He personally wielded the whip and cudgel, beating the innocent for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He personally wielded whip and cudgel, beating innocents for amusement.

sentences.zh: 穿池築觀，朝成暮毀，徵發工匠，疲極兆民。

translations.literal: He dug ponds and built towers, completing them in the morning and destroying them in the evening; he conscripted artisans until the myriad people were worn to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: He dug ponds and built towers, finishing them by morning and tearing them down by evening; he conscripted artisans until the people were worn to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 遠近歎嗟，人神怨怒，社稷將墜，豈可復嗣守洪業，君臨萬邦。

translations.literal: Near and far sighed in lament; men and spirits were angered; the altars of soil and grain were about to fall—how could he again inherit and guard the great enterprise and face the myriad states as sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far lamented; men and spirits were enraged; the altars were about to fall—how could he still inherit the great enterprise and rule the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 今廢為營陽王，一依漢昌邑、晉海西故事。

translations.literal: He is now deposed and made Prince of Yingyang, wholly following the precedents of Han’s Prince of Changyi and Jin’s Prince of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: He is now deposed and made Prince of Yingyang, following the precedents of Han’s Prince of Changyi and Jin’s Prince of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 鎮〔西將軍宜都王，仁明孝弟，著自幼辰。

translations.literal: The General Who Guards the West, the Prince of Yidu, is humane, bright, filial, and brotherly, renowned from earliest youth.
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Guards the West, Prince of Yidu, is humane, bright, filial, and brotherly, renowned from youth.

sentences.zh: 德業沖粹，識心明允。

translations.literal: His virtue and conduct are pure; his mind and judgment are clear and fair.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue is pure and his judgment clear.

sentences.zh: 宜纂洪統，光臨億兆。

translations.literal: He should inherit the great succession and shine upon the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: He should inherit the great succession and rule the hundred millions.

sentences.zh: 主者詳依典故，以時奉迎。

translations.literal: Let the responsible officials examine the statutes in detail and, at the proper time, escort him to receive the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible officials follow precedent and, at the proper time, escort him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未亡人嬰此百罹，雖存若隕。

translations.literal: I, the survivor, have met this hundredfold calamity; though I live, it is as though I had perished.
translations.idiomatic: I, who survive him, have met this hundredfold calamity; though I live, it is as though I had perished.

sentences.zh: 永悼情事，撫心摧塞。

translations.literal: Forever grieving these affairs, I press my heart and am overwhelmed.
translations.idiomatic: Forever grieving these affairs, I press my heart and am overwhelmed.

translations.literal: Closing bracket and annotation marker 16.
translations.idiomatic: Closing bracket and textual annotation marker 16.

sentences.zh: 始徐羨之、傅亮將廢帝，諷王弘、檀道濟求赴國訃。

translations.literal: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the emperor; they hinted to Wang Hong and Tan Daoji to request leave to attend the state mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang planned to depose the emperor; they urged Wang Hong and Tan Daoji to request leave for the state mourning.

sentences.zh: 弘等來朝。

translations.literal: Hong and the others came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the others came to court.

sentences.zh: 使中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛為內應。

translations.literal: They made the Palace Secretariat Attendant Xing Antai and Pan Sheng their agents within.
translations.idiomatic: They stationed Palace Secretariat attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng as agents within.

sentences.zh: 是旦，道濟、謝晦領兵居前，羨之等隨後，因東掖門開，入自雲龍門。

translations.literal: That morning, Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front; Xu Xianzhi and the others followed; when the eastern side gate opened they entered by the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That morning Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front, Xu Xianzhi and the others behind; when the eastern side gate opened they entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 盛等先戒宿衞，莫有禦者。

translations.literal: Sheng and the others had first warned the night guards; none resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and the others had first warned the night guards; none resisted.

sentences.zh: 時帝於華林園為列肆，親自酤賣。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was in Hualin Park setting up a row of shops and personally selling wine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was in Hualin Park setting up market stalls and selling wine himself.

sentences.zh: 又開瀆聚土，以象破岡埭，與左右引船唱呼，以為歡樂。

translations.literal: He also opened a channel and piled earth to imitate the Pogang dam, and with those at his side pulled boats, shouting and calling, for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened a channel and piled earth to imitate the Pogang dam, and with his companions pulled boats, shouting for sport.

sentences.zh: 夕游天淵池，即龍舟而寢。

translations.literal: In the evening he toured the Tianyuan Pool and slept on the dragon boat.
translations.idiomatic: In the evening he toured Tianyuan Pool and slept aboard the dragon boat.

sentences.zh: 其朝未興，兵士進，殺二侍者於帝側，傷帝指。

translations.literal: Before the court had risen that morning, soldiers entered, killed two attendants at the emperor’s side, and wounded his finger.
translations.idiomatic: Before court had risen that morning, soldiers entered, killed two attendants beside the emperor, and wounded his finger.

sentences.zh: 夫出東閤，就收璽紱，羣臣拜辭，送於東宮，遂幽於吳郡。

translations.literal: The husband went out through the eastern pavilion; they then took the seals and cords; the officials bowed in farewell and escorted him to the eastern palace; he was then confined in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He went out through the eastern pavilion; they took the seals and cords; officials bowed in farewell and escorted him to the eastern palace; he was then confined in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是日，赦死罪以下。

translations.literal: That day, those sentenced to death and below were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: That day, those sentenced to death or below were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 太后令奉還璽紱。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered that the seals and cords be returned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered the seals and cords returned.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟入守朝堂。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji entered to guard the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji entered to guard the court hall.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑，徐羨之等使中書舍人邢安泰弒帝於金昌亭。

translations.literal: On the day guichou in the sixth month, Xu Xianzhi and the others had the Palace Secretariat Attendant Xing Antai assassinate the emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the sixth month, Xu Xianzhi and the others had Palace Secretariat attendant Xing Antai assassinate the emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝有勇力，不即受制，突走出昌門，追以門關踣之，致殞。

translations.literal: The emperor had strength and courage and did not immediately submit; he burst out through Chang Gate, and pursuers struck him down with the gate bar, causing his death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was strong and did not submit at once; he burst out through Chang Gate, and pursuers struck him down with the gate bar and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時年十九。

translations.literal: He was nineteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was nineteen.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 17.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 17.

sentences.zh: 〈上闕〉

translations.literal: 〈Upper text missing〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The text above is missing in the received version.〉

sentences.zh: 則創業之君，自天所啟；

translations.literal: then the ruler who founds the enterprise is one Heaven itself opens;
translations.idiomatic: then the founder is one Heaven itself raises up;

sentences.zh: 守文之主，其難乎哉！

translations.literal: but for a ruler who merely keeps the written record—how hard that is!
translations.idiomatic: but for a ruler who merely keeps the written record—how hard that is!

translations.literal: Annotation marker 18.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 18.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 武帝長子也 廿二史考異云：「按紀傳書諸帝皆稱廟號，獨此紀書武帝者四，而仍有稱高祖者。

translations.literal: He was the eldest son of Emperor Wu. The Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories says: “According to the annals and biographies, all emperors are given their temple names; only this annal calls Emperor Wu by that title four times, and there are still places that call him Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He was Emperor Wu’s eldest son. Qian Daxin’s Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories says: “The annals and biographies all use temple names for emperors; only this annal calls Emperor Wu by that title four times, and there are still places that call him Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 又它篇例稱魏為索虜，而此紀一云魏軍克滑臺，一云魏主拓跋嗣薨，全非休文之例。

translations.literal: Moreover, other chapters regularly call Wei the “northern barbarians,” yet this annal once says Wei forces captured Huatai and once says the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died—altogether unlike Shen Yue’s usage.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, other chapters regularly call Wei the “northern barbarians,” yet this annal once says Wei forces captured Huatai and once says Wei ruler Tuoba Si died—nothing like Shen Yue’s usage.

sentences.zh: 又如義熙十二年正月，以豫章公世子為西中郎將、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Again, in the first month of the twelfth year of Yixi, the heir of the Duke of Yuzhang was made General of the West Center and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in the first month of Yixi year 12, the heir of the Duke of Yuzhang was made General of the West Center and Yu inspector.

sentences.zh: 三月，除征虜將軍、徐兗二州刺史，鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the third month he was relieved as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and made Inspector of Xu and Yan provinces, stationed at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was relieved as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and made inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月，除中軍將軍，副貳相國府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was relieved as General of the Center Army and made deputy to the Chancellor’s Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 14 he was relieved as General of the Center Army and made deputy to the Chancellor’s Office.

sentences.zh: 若宜見於本紀，而略不及。

translations.literal: If these ought to appear in this annal, they are altogether omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Events that ought to appear in this annal are altogether omitted.

sentences.zh: 卷末無史臣論。

translations.literal: At the end of the scroll there is no historian’s judgment.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the scroll there is no historian’s judgment.

sentences.zh: 其非休文書顯然。

translations.literal: That it is not Shen Yue’s writing is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: That this is not Shen Yue’s writing is obvious.

sentences.zh: 蓋此篇久亡，後人雜採它書以補之，故義例乖舛如此。」

translations.literal: Presumably this chapter was long lost; later men pieced it together from other books, and so its usage is so at odds."
translations.idiomatic: Presumably this chapter was long lost; later men pieced it together from other books, which is why its usage is so at odds."

sentences.zh: 年十歲拜豫章公世子 按少帝義符生於義熙二年，而據五行志授豫章世子，在義熙七年，則當云六歲，此云十歲，疑有誤。

translations.literal: At age ten he was invested as heir of the Duke of Yuzhang. According to the birth of Emperor Shao Yifu in the second year of Yixi, while according to the Treatise on the Five Phases the investiture as heir of Yuzhang was in the seventh year of Yixi, it ought to say six years old; that this says ten years is suspected to be an error.
translations.idiomatic: At age ten he was invested heir of the Duke of Yuzhang. Yifu was born in Yixi year 2, while the Treatise on the Five Phases places the Yuzhang heir investiture in Yixi year 7, so it ought to read six years old; “ten” is suspected to be an error.

sentences.zh: 辛丑祀南郊 「辛丑」各本作「辛巳」，據局本及南史改。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the southern suburb on xinchou: in all editions “xinchou” is written “xinsi”; changed according to the Bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the southern suburb on xinchou: all editions read “xinsi”; changed per the Bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按是年正月己亥朔，無辛巳，初三日辛丑。

translations.literal: According to that year’s first month, new moon on jihai—there was no xinsi; on the third day was xinchou.
translations.idiomatic: That year’s first month had its new moon on jihai; there was no xinsi; the third day was xinchou.

sentences.zh: 虜將達奚卬破金墉進圍虎牢 按據魏書奚斤傳，圍虎牢者為奚斤，斤本姓達奚氏。

translations.literal: The barbarian general Daxi Ang broke Jin Yong and advanced to besiege Hulao. According to the Wei History biography of Xi Jin, the besieger of Hulao was Xi Jin; Jin’s original surname was the Daxi clan.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Daxi Ang broke Jin Yong and besieged Hulao. According to the Wei History biography of Xi Jin, the besieger of Hulao was Xi Jin, whose clan name was originally Daxi.

sentences.zh: 「卬」當是「斤」字之譌。

translations.literal: “Ang” is probably a corruption of the character “Jin.”
translations.idiomatic: “Ang” is probably a corruption of the character “Jin.”

sentences.zh: 拓跋木末又遣安平公涉歸寇青州 拓跋木末即魏主拓跋嗣。

translations.literal: Tuoba Mumo also sent the Duke of Anping Shegui to raid Qing Province: Tuoba Mumo is the Wei ruler Tuoba Si.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Mumo also sent Duke of Anping Shegui to raid Qing Province: Tuoba Mumo is Wei ruler Tuoba Si.

sentences.zh: 本卷後又稱嗣。

translations.literal: Later in this scroll he is again called Si.
translations.idiomatic: Later in this scroll he is again called Si.

sentences.zh: 蓋所採雜異，故前後不一致。

translations.literal: Presumably because the sources gathered were mixed, the front and back are inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: The sources were evidently mixed, so the text is inconsistent throughout.

sentences.zh: 「安平公」各本作「平安公」，今從局本。

translations.literal: “Duke of Anping”: in all editions it is written “Duke of Ping’an”; now following the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: “Duke of Anping”: all editions read “Duke of Ping’an”; now following the Bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 按索虜傳：「景平元年，虜遣安平公涉歸幡能健……東擊青州。

translations.literal: According to the Account of the Northern Barbarians: “In the first year of Jingping, the barbarians sent the Duke of Anping Shegui Fannengjian… to attack east into Qing Province.”
translations.idiomatic: According to the Account of the Northern Barbarians: “In Jingping year 1, the enemy sent Duke of Anping Shegui Fannengjian… to attack east into Qing Province.”

sentences.zh: 」涉歸幡能健即叔孫建，魏書有傳，魏道武時，曾賜爵安平公。

translations.literal: ” Shegui Fannengjian is Shusun Jian; the Wei History has his biography; in the time of Emperor Daowu of Wei he was once granted the rank of Duke of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shegui Fannengjian is Shusun Jian; the Wei History has his biography; under Emperor Daowu of Wei he had once been granted the rank Duke of Anping.

sentences.zh: 庚辰 張熷讀史舉正云：「二月丁丑、庚辰書辛未前，誤。

translations.literal: Gengchen. Zhang Huang’s Corrections in Reading History says: “In the second month, dingchou and gengchen are recorded before xinwei—an error.”
translations.idiomatic: Gengchen. Zhang Huang’s Corrections in Reading History says: “In the second month, dingchou and gengchen are recorded before xinwei—an error.”

sentences.zh: 」按張說是。

translations.literal: ” According to Zhang, this is correct.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang’s view is correct.

sentences.zh: 二月戊辰朔，初四日辛未，初十日丁丑，十三日庚辰，辛未不當在庚辰後。

translations.literal: The second month’s new moon was on wuchen; the fourth day was xinwei, the tenth day dingchou, the thirteenth day gengchen—xinwei cannot come after gengchen.
translations.idiomatic: The second month’s new moon was wuchen; the fourth day was xinwei, the tenth dingchou, the thirteenth gengchen—xinwei cannot come after gengchen.

sentences.zh: 爵蒙遜為驃騎大將軍 各本皆無「驃騎」二字。

translations.literal: Enfeoffing Mengxun as General of Agile Cavalry: in all editions the two characters “Agile Cavalry” are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffing Mengxun as General of Agile Cavalry: all editions lack the two characters “Agile Cavalry.”

sentences.zh: 按本書文帝紀，元嘉二年，驃騎大將軍涼州牧大沮渠蒙遜改為車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: According to the Annals of Emperor Wen in this book, in the second year of Yuanjia, the General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Liang Province, the great Juqu Mengxun, was changed to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: According to this book’s Annals of Emperor Wen, in Yuanjia year 2, General of Agile Cavalry and Liang governor the great Juqu Mengxun was changed to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 則各本並奪「驃騎」二字。

translations.literal: Thus all editions together omit the two characters “Agile Cavalry.”
translations.idiomatic: Thus all editions together omit “Agile Cavalry.”

sentences.zh: 今據南史補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Now supplemented from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 富陽人孫法光反 「孫法光」，褚叔度傳作「孫法亮」。

translations.literal: Sun Faguang of Fuyang rebelled: “Sun Faguang” in the biography of Chu Shudu is written “Sun Faliang.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Faguang of Fuyang rebelled: the biography of Chu Shudu has “Sun Faliang.”

sentences.zh: 會稽太守褚淡之遣山陰令陸劭討敗之 「褚淡之」各本並作「褚談」，據褚叔度傳，時會稽太守為褚淡之，「談」蓋「淡」之形譌。

translations.literal: The Governor of Kuaiji Chu Danzhi sent the Magistrate of Shanyin Lu Shao to attack and defeat him: “Chu Danzhi” in all editions is written “Chu Tan”; according to the biography of Chu Shudu, at the time the Governor of Kuaiji was Chu Danzhi—“Tan” is probably a graphic corruption of “Dan.”
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji governor Chu Danzhi sent Shanyin magistrate Lu Shao to defeat him: all editions read “Chu Tan”; Chu Shudu’s biography shows the Kuaiji governor was Chu Danzhi—“Tan” is probably a corruption of “Dan.”

sentences.zh: 按南北朝人名後之「之」字，有時可以省去。

translations.literal: According to personal names of the Northern and Southern Dynasties, the final character zhi is sometimes omitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern and Southern Dynasties personal names, the final character zhi is sometimes omitted.

sentences.zh: 今仍改「談」作「淡」，並補「之」字。

translations.literal: Now “Tan” is still changed to “Dan,” and the character zhi is restored.
translations.idiomatic: “Tan” is changed to “Dan” and the character zhi restored.

sentences.zh: 殺虜潁川太守庾龍 「潁川」各本並作「潁州」，據劉粹傳改。

translations.literal: Killed the barbarian Administrator of Yingchuan Yu Long: “Yingchuan” in all editions is written “Yingzhou”; changed according to the biography of Liu Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Killed the enemy Yingchuan administrator Yu Long: all editions read “Yingzhou”; changed per Liu Cui’s biography.

sentences.zh: 以旱詔赦五歲刑以下罪人 各本並脫「刑」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Edict pardoning offenders of five years’ punishment and below because of drought: in all editions the character “punishment” is missing; supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Edict pardoning those sentenced to five years or less because of drought: all editions omit “punishment”; supplemented from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅 按景平元年十二月癸巳朔，無丙寅。

translations.literal: Twelfth month bingyin: according to Jingping year 1, the twelfth month’s new moon was on guisi—there was no bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month bingyin: in Jingping year 1 the twelfth month’s new moon was guisi—there was no bingyin.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月癸巳朔日有蝕之 「二月癸巳朔」，局本同，宋本、北監本、毛本、殿本、通鑑考異引宋略、建康實錄作「正月癸巳朔」，南史宋本紀作「二月己卯朔」。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, second month, new moon guisi, eclipse of the sun: “second month, new moon guisi”—the Bureau edition agrees; the Song, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Zizhi Tongjian Examination citing Song Lüe and Jiankang shilu have “first month, new moon guisi”; the Annals in the Song edition of the History of the Southern Dynasties has “second month, new moon jimao.”
translations.idiomatic: Year 2, spring, second month, new moon guisi, solar eclipse: “second month, new moon guisi”—the Bureau edition agrees; Song, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace editions and Zizhi Tongjian Examination citing Song Lüe and Jiankang shilu have “first month, new moon guisi”; the Song annals in the History of the Southern Dynasties has “second month, new moon jimao.”

sentences.zh: 按陳垣朔閏表，景平二年正月癸亥朔，二月壬辰朔。

translations.literal: According to Chen Yuan’s table of new moons and intercalations, in Jingping year 2 the first month’s new moon was on guihai and the second month’s on renchen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuan’s table of new moons and intercalations gives Jingping year 2 first month new moon guihai and second month renchen.

sentences.zh: 查正月無癸巳，癸巳為二月初二日。

translations.literal: Checking: the first month has no guisi; guisi is the second day of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: The first month has no guisi; guisi is the second day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 然日蝕當在朔日，是年正月祇二十九日，作二月壬辰朔者，蓋後人定朔有誤。

translations.literal: Yet a solar eclipse should fall on the new-moon day; that year the first month had only twenty-nine days—those who make the second month’s new moon renchen probably erred in fixing the new moon later.
translations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse should fall on the new-moon day; that year the first month had only twenty-nine days—making the second month’s new moon renchen probably reflects a later error in fixing the calendar.

sentences.zh: 宋書五行志作「二月癸巳朔」。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases in the Song History has “second month, new moon guisi.”
translations.idiomatic: The Song History Treatise on the Five Phases has “second month, new moon guisi.”

sentences.zh: 今改從局本。

translations.literal: Now following the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: The text now follows the Bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 乙未以皇弟義恭為冠軍將軍南豫州刺史乙巳大風 按陳垣朔閏表景平二年正月癸亥朔，是月無乙未、乙巳。

translations.literal: Yiwei: the emperor’s younger brother Yigong made General Who Crowns the Army and Inspector of South Yu; yisi: great wind. According to Chen Yuan’s table, Jingping year 2 first month new moon guihai—that month had no yiwei or yisi.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwei: younger brother Yigong made General Who Crowns the Army and South Yu inspector; yisi: great wind. Chen Yuan’s table gives Jingping year 2 first month new moon guihai—that month had no yiwei or yisi.

sentences.zh: 二月壬辰朔，初三日乙未，十三日乙巳。

translations.literal: The second month’s new moon was renchen; the third day was yiwei, the thirteenth day yisi.
translations.idiomatic: The second month’s new moon was renchen; the third day was yiwei, the thirteenth yisi.

sentences.zh: 可證上之春正月應作春二月。

translations.literal: This proves that the “first month of spring” above should read “second month of spring.”
translations.idiomatic: This shows the “first month of spring” above should read “second month of spring.”

sentences.zh: 江州刺史王弘南兗州刺史檀道濟入朝 各本並作「江州刺史檀道濟、揚州刺史王弘入朝」。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jiang Province Wang Hong and the Inspector of South Yan Province Tan Daoji entered court: in all editions it is written “the Inspector of Jiang Province Tan Daoji and the Inspector of Yang Province Wang Hong entered court.”
translations.idiomatic: Jiang inspector Wang Hong and South Yan inspector Tan Daoji entered court: all editions read “Jiang inspector Tan Daoji and Yang inspector Wang Hong entered court.”

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「江州刺史王弘、南兗州刺史檀道濟來朝」，是，今據改。

translations.literal: The Jiankang shilu has “the Inspector of Jiang Province Wang Hong and the Inspector of South Yan Province Tan Daoji came to court,” which is correct; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang shilu has “Jiang inspector Wang Hong and South Yan inspector Tan Daoji came to court,” which is correct; the text is changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 錢大昕廿二史考異云：「按是時道濟為南兗州刺史，非江州；

translations.literal: Qian Daxin’s Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories says: “According to this time Tan Daoji was Inspector of South Yan, not Jiang;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin’s Examination says: “At this time Tan Daoji was South Yan inspector, not Jiang;

sentences.zh: 弘為江州刺史，非揚州也。

translations.literal: Hong was Inspector of Jiang, not Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was Jiang inspector, not Yang.

sentences.zh: 揚州治輦下，時以司空徐羨之領之。

translations.literal: Yang Province’s seat was the capital district; at the time the Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi held it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province governed the capital; Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi held it concurrently.

sentences.zh: 紀所書皆誤。」

translations.literal: What the annal records is all wrong.”
translations.idiomatic: What the annal records is all wrong.”

sentences.zh: 西將軍宜都王

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West, Prince of Yidu
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the West, Prince of Yidu

translations.literal: 〈To〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈To〉

sentences.zh: 撫心摧塞 各本並脫，今據元龜一八八補。

translations.literal: Press the heart and are overwhelmed: in all editions this is missing; now supplemented according to Yuan gui 188.
translations.idiomatic: “Press the heart and are overwhelmed”: missing in all editions; now supplemented from Yuan gui 188.

sentences.zh: 始徐羨之傅亮將廢帝

translations.literal: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the emperor
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang planned to depose the emperor

translations.literal: 〈To〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈To〉

sentences.zh: 時年十九 此段宋本巳有脫葉。

translations.literal: He was nineteen years old: this passage in the Song edition already had lacunae.
translations.idiomatic: He was nineteen: this passage already had lacunae in the Song edition.

sentences.zh: 北監本、毛本、殿本、局本據南史補。

translations.literal: The Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions supplemented from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 今仍錄存。

translations.literal: It is still recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: It is still recorded here.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮、檀道濟、謝晦等入雲龍門至華林園廢少帝一段，又見沈約宋書徐羨之傳中。

translations.literal: The passage in which Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji, Xie Hui, and others entered the Cloud Dragon Gate as far as Hualin Park to depose Emperor Shao also appears in Shen Yue’s Song History, biography of Xu Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The passage in which Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji, Xie Hui, and others entered the Cloud Dragon Gate to Hualin Park to depose Emperor Shao also appears in Shen Yue’s Song History biography of Xu Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 天淵池，各本作天泉池，蓋據李延壽南史，乃避唐諱。

translations.literal: Tianyuan Pool: in all editions it is written Tianquan Pool, probably following Li Yanshou’s History of the Southern Dynasties to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyuan Pool: all editions read Tianquan Pool, probably following Li Yanshou’s History of the Southern Dynasties to avoid Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 今仍據沈約宋書徐羨之傳改為天淵池。

translations.literal: Now it is still changed to Tianyuan Pool according to Shen Yue’s Song History biography of Xu Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The text now reads Tianyuan Pool per Shen Yue’s Song History biography of Xu Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 其難乎哉 各本並脫此一行，僅涵芬樓影印百衲本所據之宋本，有此殘葉。

translations.literal: How hard that is: in all editions this line is missing; only the Song edition used by the Hanfenlou photolithograph of the Baona edition has this surviving leaf.
translations.idiomatic: “How hard that is”: all editions lack this line; only the Song edition underlying the Hanfenlou Baona photolithograph preserves this surviving leaf.

sentences.zh: 蓋即本卷史臣曰之殘存結尾語。

translations.literal: Presumably it is the surviving closing words of this scroll’s historian’s judgment.
translations.idiomatic: It is presumably the surviving closing line of this scroll’s historian’s judgment.
